title: True Beauty, Vol. 1
description: Bullied for her appearance, high schooler Jugyeong Lim masters makeup via online tutorials, transforming overnight into a school celebrity goddess. Anxiously guarding her bare-faced secret, she finds herself drawn into a love triangle.

title: Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint, Vol. 1
description: Office worker Dokja Kim is the sole reader to complete an obscure 3,000-chapter web novel. When the fictional apocalypse becomes brutal reality on his subway ride home, Dokja utilizes his omniscient story knowledge to survive the first scenario.

title: Villains Are Destined to Die, Vol. 1
description: A young woman reincarnates into an otome game as Penelope Eckhart, the villainous adopted daughter doomed to die at every turn. To avoid execution, she must carefully raise love affection gauges with unpredictable male leads.

title: Maus I: A Survivor's Tale: My Father Bleeds History
description: The Pulitzer Prize-winning graphic novel depicting Art Spiegelman interviewing his Polish Jewish father Vladek about surviving the Holocaust. Depicting Jews as mice and Nazis as cats, the work addresses survivor guilt and generational memory.

title: Maus II: A Survivor's Tale: And Here My Troubles Began
description: The concluding installment of Spiegelman's Holocaust testimony following Vladek and Anja inside Auschwitz and Dachau death camps, alongside Art's own struggles processing his father's trauma and commercial success.

title: Persepolis: The Story of a Childhood
description: An insightful graphic memoir recounting Marjane Satrapi's childhood in Tehran during the Islamic Revolution and Iran-Iraq War. With stark, expressive black-and-white art, it captures childhood rebellion and sociopolitical upheaval.

title: Persepolis 2: The Story of a Return
description: The sequel chronicling Marjane's high school years in Vienna as an Iranian expatriate, grappling with alienation and cultural dislocation, followed by her bittersweet return to university in repressive Tehran.

title: Fun Home: A Family Tragicomic
description: Alison Bechdel's graphic memoir investigating her relationship with her closeted, emotionally distant English teacher and funeral director father, who died shortly after Alison came out as lesbian.

title: Blankets
description: A sweeping autobiographical graphic novel chronicling Craig Thompson's childhood in rural evangelical Wisconsin, his sibling bond, and his bittersweet first love with a girl named Raina during winter camp.

title: Heartstopper: Volume 1
description: A sweet British LGBTQ+ coming-of-age graphic novel following openly gay overthinker Charlie Spring and rugby player Nick Nelson as they become desk partners and discover budding romantic feelings.

title: Heartstopper: Volume 2
description: Nick comes to terms with his bisexuality and feelings for Charlie while worrying about coming out to his rugby friends. A gentle exploration of self-discovery, friendship, and first dates.

title: Heartstopper: Volume 3
description: Charlie and Nick travel to Paris on a school trip where their relationship grows stronger, while addressing Charlie's mental health struggles and eating disorder with compassion and care.

title: Nimona
description: Nimona, an impulsive young shapeshifter, becomes the sidekick to supervillain Lord Ballister Blackheart to expose the dark underbelly of the Institution of Law Enforcement and Heroics.

title: Saga, Vol. 1
description: Two soldiers from warring extraterrestrial races, winged Alana and horned Marko, fall in love and risk everything to raise their newborn daughter Hazel across an unforgiving galaxy.

title: Saga, Vol. 2
description: As bounty hunters and imperial forces pursue Marko and Alana across the cosmos, they make an unexpected landing on the planetoid Quietus to meet a favorite reclusive romance novelist.

title: Daytripper
description: Brás de Oliva Domingos is an aspiring Brazilian novelist writing obituaries for a São Paulo newspaper. Each chapter portrays a pivotal day in Brás's life ending with his death at different ages, celebrating the beauty of mortality.

title: Ghost World
description: Best friends Enid Coleslaw and Rebecca Doppelmeyer drift cynically through post-high school suburban summer, observing bizarre local characters while feeling their own close friendship slowly unravel.

title: Understanding Comics: The Invisible Art
description: A comic book about comics analyzing the formal grammar, visual iconography, and storytelling power of sequential art. Scott McCloud explores closure between panels, time representation, and pictorial abstraction.

title: The Very Hungry Caterpillar
description: A beloved board book classic following the appetite and transformation of a small caterpillar into a beautiful butterfly. Featuring iconic die-cut pages and vibrant collage artwork that teach counting and days of the week.

title: Goodnight Moon
description: A gentle bedtime rhyming ritual bidding goodnight to every familiar object in the great green room. Clement Hurd's soothing alternating color and black-and-white illustrations lull infants and toddlers to sleep.

title: Dear Zoo
description: An engaging lift-the-flap board book where a child writes to the zoo asking for a pet. Young toddlers discover why elephants are too big, giraffes are too tall, and lions are too fierce before finding the perfect puppy.

title: Brown Bear, Brown Bear, What Do You See?
description: A rhythmic question-and-response favorite introducing a parade of colorful animals and cheerful characters. Designed with bright tissue-paper collages to build early color recognition and language association.

title: Where's Spot?
description: The original lift-the-flap adventure where Sally the dog searches behind doors, inside clocks, and under stairs for her mischievous puppy Spot. A timeless interactive reading treat for toddlers.

title: Peek-a Who?
description: Colorful die-cut peek-a-boo windows provide visual hints for rhyming answers including cows, ghosts, and trains, finishing with a mirror surprise for the toddler reading along.

title: Guess How Much I Love You
description: Little Nutbrown Hare and Big Nutbrown Hare playfully measure their boundless love for one another across fields, rivers, and all the way to the moon and back. Soft watercolor illustrations complement a tender bedtime story.

title: Pajama Time!
description: An upbeat, sing-along bedtime board book featuring an assortment of dancing animals jumping into their favorite pajamas as the moon rises. Sandra Boynton's trademark rhymes make bedtime energetic yet cozy.

title: Moo, Baa, La La La!
description: A hilarious introduction to barnyard animal sounds where pigs say "la la la" instead of "oink." Toddlers delight in chiming in and correcting the silly animals.

title: Ten Little Fingers and Ten Little Toes
description: Babies born in different lands across town and country share one wonderful thing in common: ten little fingers and ten sweet little toes. A joyful global celebration of infancy and maternal love.

title: Where the Wild Things Are
description: Sent to his bedroom without supper for mischief, young Max sails across the ocean to the land of the Wild Things and becomes their king. A celebrated Caldecott Medalist exploring childhood imagination and emotional self-soothing.

title: The Giving Tree
description: A memorable parable about the lifelong bond between an apple tree and a growing boy who continually takes from her shade, apples, branches, and trunk. Shel Silverstein's sparse line art provokes thoughtful conversations on generosity.

title: Green Eggs and Ham
publisher: Random House Books for Young Readers
description: Sam-I-Am persistently invites a skeptical friend to sample a platter of green eggs and ham in a house, with a mouse, in a box, and with a fox. Written using only fifty distinct vocabulary words to encourage early reading confidence.

title: The Cat in the Hat
publisher: Random House Books for Young Readers
description: Left alone on a cold rainy day, Sally and her brother are visited by an eccentric cat wearing a striped stovepipe hat who turns their quiet household upside down with Thing One and Thing Two.

title: Room on the Broom
description: A friendly witch and her cat fly happily across the sky until wind blows away her hat, bow, and wand. Helpful animal companions retrieve the lost items and earn a spot on the broomstick, uniting to scare away a hungry dragon.

title: The Gruffalo
description: A clever little mouse takes a stroll through the deep dark wood, scaring off predatory foxes, owls, and snakes by inventing tales of a terrifying beast called a Gruffalo—until he bumps straight into one.

title: We're Going on a Bear Hunt
description: An intrepid family ventures out on a glorious day to catch a big bear, swishing through long grass, squelching through thick mud, and braving a swirling snowstorm before retreating home under the duvet.

title: Corduroy
description: A department store teddy bear missing a button on his green overalls embarks on a nighttime quest across furniture escalators to find it, hoping a child will finally adopt him. A warm classic celebrating friendship.

title: The Day the Crayons Quit
description: Duncan reaches for his crayon box only to find a packet of humorous protest letters from overworked Blue, underappreciated White, and squabbling Yellow and Orange. Winner of numerous illustrated picture book honors.

title: If You Give a Mouse a Cookie
description: A charming circular cause-and-effect story about an energetic little mouse who asks for a glass of milk to go with his cookie, then a straw, a napkin, a mirror, and a haircut.

title: Frog and Toad Are Friends
description: Five timeless episodic tales celebrating the quiet, loyal companionship of optimistic Frog and grumpy Toad across spring swimming, letter writing, and button hunts. An I Can Read Book classic.

title: An Elephant & Piggie Biggie!
description: A bumper bind-up of five hilarious comic-dialogue adventures between anxious elephant Gerald and cheerful pig Piggie. Expressive speech bubbles and minimal text foster independent reading enjoyment.

title: Amelia Bedelia
description: The delightfully literal-minded housekeeper Amelia Bedelia dusts the furniture with dusting powder and dresses the chicken in little outfits, saving the day with a delicious lemon meringue pie.

title: Little Bear
description: Four comforting chapters following Little Bear on imaginative adventures, from flying to the moon to making birthday soup, always supported by Mother Bear's warm presence and tender care.

title: Henry and Mudge: The First Book
description: Lonely only child Henry gains a loyal English Mastiff puppy named Mudge who quickly grows to 180 pounds. Together they share autumn walks and comforting companion routines in a friendly neighborhood setting.

title: Nate the Great
description: Pancake-loving boy detective Nate takes on the perplexing case of his friend Annie's missing yellow picture of a dog. Marc Simont's whimsical illustrations accompany this early chapter-book mystery classic.

title: Mercy Watson to the Rescue
description: To the Watson family, Mercy is not just a pig—she is a porcine wonder with an immense passion for buttered toast. When the floor collapses under the Watsons' bed, Mercy sets off an accidental neighbourhood rescue.

title: Hi! Fly Guy
description: A boy named Buzz catches a pet fly that can say his name: "BUZZ!" Buzz enters his ingenious insect companion into the local Amazing Pet Show to prove flies are the smartest creatures around.

title: Biscuit
description: Time for bed, but sweet yellow puppy Biscuit wants a snack, a drink of water, another blanket, and one more goodnight hug. Simple repetition and warm illustrations support emergent decoders.

title: Penny and Her Song
description: Little mouse Penny comes home from school with a wonderful song she composed herself, but must wait until her baby siblings wake from their nap before performing for the whole family.

title: Wonder
description: August Pullman, a ten-year-old boy born with facial differences, enters Beecher Prep for his first year of regular school. Told from multiple viewpoints, the novel champions empathy, courage, and choosing kindness.

title: The Lightning Thief
description: Twelve-year-old dyslexic Percy Jackson discovers his absent father is Poseidon, Greek god of the sea. Accused of stealing Zeus's master lightning bolt, Percy quests across America to prevent an Olympian war.
